series.name: Core CPI m/m
series.source_caveat: Anything stamped MODELED is a construction, not an observation.

movers.name: Mortgage / 10Y Treasury Spread
movers.notes: MORT30Y minus UST10Y. The single most important spread on the screen.

movers.name: Brent Crude (global benchmark)
movers.notes: Brent Europe spot FOB. The global benchmark: prices roughly two thirds of the world’s traded crude, and it is waterborne, so it carries geopolitical and freight risk that WTI does not.

movers.name: WTI Crude (US benchmark)
movers.notes: West Texas Intermediate, Cushing OK spot FOB. The US benchmark: light, sweet, landlocked. Prices domestic refinery input and therefore US gasoline.

drivers.name: Mortgage spread (w/w)
drivers.detail: Published spread moved +6 bp between PMMS prints

drivers.name: 10Y Treasury
drivers.detail: 10Y -1 bp, passed through at a 0.95 beta

drivers.name: Fed expectations (2Y)
drivers.detail: 2Y +2 bp. The front end is the cleanest free read on Fed repricing while futures probabilities are unavailable.

drivers.name: Average Hourly Earnings
drivers.detail: Average Hourly Earnings 3.02 vs trailing 24m mean (-2.5 sigma). Very bullish for rates

drivers.name: Consumer Price Index
drivers.detail: Consumer Price Index 3.72 vs trailing 24m mean (1.8 sigma). Very bearish for rates

drivers.name: Brent crude (global)
drivers.detail: Brent $-5.00 (-2.3 sigma). The global benchmark, so it moves world inflation expectations and therefore demand for US duration. It also cuts the other way through recession risk, and the engine nets both channels.  extreme move: bigger than 96% of history.

bullets.text: 10-year Treasury at 4.99%, -1 bp on the day. This is the single biggest input to your rate.
Published 30-year survey at 7.32%, -8 bp week over week. It is a weekly average and always lags your rate sheet.
Mortgage spread 236 bp, normal at the 69th percentile of 10 years. That is 2.36 points of the 7.32% rate coming from spread, not from Treasuries.
Brent Crude $-5.00, bigger than 96% of moves on record. Watch whether the bond market trades this as inflation or as demand.

upcoming.name: Initial Jobless Claims
upcoming.why: A hotter than expected print pushes mortgage rates down.

upcoming.name: FOMC Rate Decision
upcoming.why: The statement and any dot plot revision move the 2Y, which pulls the 10Y and then mortgage rates.

upcoming.name: Initial Jobless Claims
upcoming.why: A hotter than expected print pushes mortgage rates down.

upcoming.name: Nonfarm Payrolls
upcoming.why: Strong jobs means stronger growth, less Fed easing, higher yields.

alerts.label: Crude benchmark moved at an extreme percentile
alerts.why: An energy shock hits mortgage rates through two channels at once. It lifts inflation expectations, which pushes the 10Y and your rate UP, and it raises recession risk, which pushes them DOWN. Watch which one the bond market picks. If the 10Y sells off with crude, the market is trading inflation and you should protect float positions.
